title: ⚛️ How to Build Reusable React Components?
excerpt: Each product needs an image, title, price, and an "Add to Cart" button.
body:
ㅤ 📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 07 ㅤ Imagine building an e-commerce website with hundreds of products. Each product needs an image, title, price, and an "Add to Cart" button. Would you write the same code for every product? 🤔 Of course not! That's where React component architecture becomes useful. Let's break it down! 👇 ㅤ 1️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝗮 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁? 🧩 A component is a reusable piece of UI. Instead of building an entire page in one file, we divide it into smaller components. For example: 🏠 HomePage ├── Navbar ├── ProductList │ └── ProductCard └── Footer Each component has a clear responsibility. ㅤ 2️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗥𝗲𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀? ♻️ Imagine displaying 100 products. Instead of writing 100 separate UI blocks, we can create one ProductCard component and reuse it. ✅ Less duplicated code ✅ Easier maintenance ✅ Consistent UI ✅ Faster development ㅤ 3️⃣ 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗽𝘀 — 𝗣𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 📦 Props allow parent components to pass data to child components. Example: function ProductCard({ name, price }) { return (

{name}

${price}

); } Usage: The same component can display different products using different props. ㅤ 4️⃣ 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 — 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀 🔄 State allows a component to remember information between renders. For example: const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(1); When the quantity changes, React updates the relevant UI. Props → Data received from a parent State → Data managed by a component ㅤ 5️⃣ 𝗞𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 🎯 A good component should have a clear purpose. For example: ✅ ProductCard → Displays product details ✅ SearchBar → Handles search input ✅ CartButton → Handles cart interaction ✅ ProductList → Renders product cards Smaller, focused components are easier to test and maintain. ㅤ 💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 Good React architecture isn't just about splitting code into multiple files. It's about building components that are reusable, readable, and easy to maintain. Understanding props, state, and component responsibilities helps us build scalable frontend applications. ㅤ 💬 What's your approach to organizing React components in large projects? ㅤ #ReactJS #SoftwareEngineering #FrontendDevelopment #JavaScript #WebDevelopment
